title: Fink on Warhol: New York Photographs of the 1960s

description.main: Previously unpublished photographs of Andy Warhol and his circle, made by Larry Fink over a few days in spring 1966.
description.extended:
Previously unpublished photographs of Andy Warhol and his circle, made by Larry Fink over four or five days in the spring of 1966.

Fink shot the pictures on assignment for the literary magazine East Side Review, which closed before they ran. The book prints them for the first time, together with other Warhol photographs from the period. The sitters include Ingrid Superstar, Lou Reed, John Cale, Edie Sedgwick and Gerard Malanga, photographed on the Lower East Side. Fink calls the shoot spontaneous and says he never thought to publish the pictures. Kevin Moore contributes the text.

Fink (b. 1941) is best known for the photobook Social Graces (1984), which set working-class Pennsylvania against upper-crust Manhattan. He has taught at Yale, Cooper Union, Parsons and Tyler School of Art, and is professor of photography at Bard College.
